Original Windows 1.2 help · English adaptation

Tower of the Sorcerer

The adventurer’s handbook

A thoughtful climb through fifty floors. Learn the rules, choose your battles, and keep a few surprises for the journey.

01 — 50Every step is a decision

Chapter 01

Before you enter the tower

A hero enters a tower to rescue a captive princess. It sounds familiar, but the original authors warn that the story may not unfold as you expect. Discover the reason as you play.

Tower of the Sorcerer sits between a role-playing game and a puzzle. There is no random element: the same actions in the same situation produce the same result. Take your time, think ahead, and choose the order in which you spend health, gold and keys.

Reading this edition

The main explanations are adapted from the original manuals. Boxes marked “Rust remake” describe this version; boxes marked “Rule clarification” explain a detail established by the project’s original-executable research. The original Windows setup and controls are retained below for reference.

Based on: TSW.txt, “The story” / Tsw.hlp, “The story & Setting up The Game”

Chapter 02

Movement, items and saving

Rust remake · current controls

Move with the arrow keys or WASD, or click a destination on the map. Click routes follow clear roads and stop at obstacles; selecting an enemy or door directly can make it the final action. Use the inventory to activate items, and Enter or Space to advance dialogue. Settings contains language, audio, animation speed and portable-save options.

Rust remake · saves

Accepted game actions autosave. “Save game” keeps a separate checkpoint, and “Restore checkpoint” returns to it. The original text manual says saving requires the Hero Orb; this remake permits saving before you obtain it. The orb is still required for detailed enemy forecasts.

Original Windows 1.2 setup and controls
  • At first launch, choose mouse or keyboard mode, font size, and a save directory. The default mode is mouse, and saves go in the installation’s SAVEDAT folder.
  • The original menu switches between 640 × 400 and 800 × 500 display sizes. TSW.txt also mentions the TSW12.INI settings file in the Windows directory.
  • With the mouse, click the direction buttons at the bottom right to move, the upper menu to save, and item icons to use them.
  • With the keyboard, use the arrow keys to move, Alt to select a menu, Enter to begin selecting an item, the arrow keys to choose it, and Escape to cancel.

Based on: TSW.txt, “Setting Up TSW” and “Playing the game” / Tsw.hlp, “How to Play”; remake README

Chapter 03

Understanding your status

What the original status indicators mean
IndicatorMeaning
FloorYour current place in the fifty-floor tower.
Health · HPDamage reduces health; reaching zero ends the game. Potions and altar offerings restore it. The manual gives no upper limit.
Attack · ATKDetermines how much damage you deal. Red crystals, swords and altar offerings increase it.
Defense · DEFReduces damage from ordinary attacks. Blue crystals, shields and altar offerings increase it.
GoldEarned by defeating enemies. Spend it at altars or trade with merchants.
KeysOpening a colored door spends one key of the matching color: yellow, blue or red.
EquipmentThe weapon and shield displays show your current equipment. Swords raise attack; shields raise defense.
InventoryShows the special items you have collected. Select an item to use its ability.
InformationEnemy information, status messages and conversations explain what is happening around you.

The help file calls the middle key color “purple”, while TSW.txt calls it “blue”. This handbook uses blue, matching the remake’s labels.

Based on: TSW.txt, “The screen and the rule and parameter explanation” / Tsw.hlp, screen hotspots

Chapter 04

Think before you fight

Walking into an enemy begins a battle. In an ordinary battle, you strike first, then the enemy retaliates. Attacks alternate until one side reaches zero health. If you win, you take the enemy’s gold.

Ordinary battles, without an item multiplier. HP = health · ATK = attack · DEF = defense. Your values are green; the enemy’s values are red.

01 · Your damage per hit

Hero ATK−Enemy DEF

Your base attack must be greater than the enemy’s defense to begin the fight.

02 · Damage from one enemy retaliation

max(Enemy ATK−Hero DEF,0)

max means “take the larger value”. If your defense blocks the attack, you lose no HP.

03 · Number of enemy retaliations

⌊Enemy HP−1Your damage per hit⌋

⌊ ⌋ means round down. The enemy does not retaliate after your killing blow.

04 · Total health lost

Retaliations×Damage per retaliation

Use the results of steps 02 and 03.

05 · The survival check

Hero HP>Total health lost

Equal is not enough: reaching zero HP is fatal. Special encounters may strike first or follow scripted rules.

Worked example · a three-hit victory

Hero

ATK 15 · DEF 12 · HP to be checked

Example enemy

HP 30 · ATK 18 · DEF 5

  1. Your damage per hit15 − 5 = 10 HP
  2. Damage per retaliation18 − 12 = 6 HP
  3. Enemy retaliations⌊ (30 − 1) ÷ 10 ⌋ = 2
  4. Total health lost2 × 6 = 12 HP

You need at least 13 HP to survive. At 13 HP, you finish with 1 HP.

The original manual reminds you that the Cross and similar equipment affect only certain creatures. Their extra strength is not a universal increase against every enemy.

Based on: TSW.txt, “On Battle” / Tsw.hlp, “Fighting Explanation & About Fairies”; docs/mechanics.md

Chapter 05

Spend your strength wisely

You cannot win simply by killing every creature and collecting every item. A treasure may be visible but expensive to reach. Decide what to collect now, what to leave for later, and which enemies you can avoid.

  • Avoid unnecessary fights, especially before your equipment improves.
  • Compare the health cost of a route with the strength or resources it gives you.
  • Return to earlier floors when improved attack or defense makes their enemies cheaper to defeat.
  • Listen to people in the tower. Information that seems unhelpful now may matter later.

Based on: TSW.txt, “How to conquer this game” / Tsw.hlp, “How to win the game”

Chapter 06

Special items

The original help introduces seven of the tower’s fifteen special items. Their descriptions encourage experimentation; acquisition hints are folded away below.

Orb of the Hero · Hero Orb

Compares your strength with an enemy’s and forecasts the battle result. Remember that the Cross and similar items help only against the creatures they affect.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

Speak with the old man on floor 3.

Orb of Wisdom

Remembers the important information you have heard. Reviewing it later can make a previously puzzling clue understandable. It is a different item from the Hero Orb.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

It is on floor 6, guarded by Skeleton B.

Orb of Flight · Orb of Flying

Use it beside stairs to travel to floors you have already visited. It can be used repeatedly without being exhausted, saving you the climb back through familiar passages.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

It is on floor 1, guarded by Skeleton B.

Magic Mattock

Makes openings in the walls around you. The help suggests trying different places: an unexpected opening may be more valuable than a direct route.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

TSW.txt says it appears after defeating the Giant Octopus on floor 16.

Magic Elixir

Restores health according to your attack and defense at the moment you drink it. Its timing matters: using it after becoming stronger can yield more health.

Acquisition hint · spoiler

The text manual hints that someone already has it and may be willing to give it to you.

Destruction Ball · “destructible ball”

A bomb for destroying enemies around you, including opponents too costly to fight normally. It does not work against every enemy. The help file specifies enemies on the surrounding sides, rather than all enemies on the floor.

Warp Staff · Space Staff

Moves you to another place on the same floor. Like the Mattock, it can reveal surprising ways through the tower. The original help describes the destination as random or unknown.

Rule clarification · destination

The original executable actually mirrors your position through the center of the 11 × 11 map: using zero-based coordinates, (x, y) becomes (10 − x, 10 − y). The destination must be ordinary road. A charge is spent even when that destination is blocked. The remake follows this deterministic rule.

Based on: TSW.txt, “The explanation of the special items” / Tsw.hlp, “Special Item Explanation”; docs/mechanics.md

Chapter 07

The fairies’ appraisal

In the original game, clearing a major area brings out a fairy. She appraises your progress using your remaining health, attack, defense and keys. Keeping resources matters beyond merely surviving the next battle.

Rust remake · fairy behavior

The remake has the fairy’s continue interaction and normal saving, but the original score/rank tables and automatic fairy checkpoint files are not yet reproduced. Do not rely on a fairy visit to create a checkpoint; use “Save game” when you want one.

Based on: TSW.txt, “About fairies” / Tsw.hlp, “Fighting Explanation & About Fairies”; docs/mechanics.md

Chapter 08

A route through the first area

The authors included an opening route to help you learn the game. It is one suggested approach, not a promise that every custom campaign follows the same route.

Reveal the original floor 1–10 walkthrough · spoilers

Avoid unnecessary fights. In particular, do not fight the armed Skeleton before obtaining a shield.

  1. After the introduction, head for floor 5 and collect its sword. Check the walls for a secret passage.
  2. Offer gold at the altar on floor 4 to raise defense.
  3. Gather the crystals on floors 1–5, then offer at the altar again to improve defense.
  4. Collect the shield on floor 9.
  5. Gather crystals throughout floors 1–10. Defeat enemies that cannot hurt you, collect their gold, and improve attack and defense at the altar.
  6. When ready, defeat the floor-8 gatekeepers and obtain the red key, then challenge the Skeleton boss on floor 10. The manual suggests that one blue key and five yellow keys may be left uncollected if necessary.

Experiment while learning. As the rules become familiar, you can work out a shorter or more efficient route yourself.

Based on: TSW.txt, “First Area Walk-through” / Tsw.hlp, “How to win the game”

Chapter 09

The five regions of the tower

The original help divides the tower into five ten-floor regions. Its summaries reveal enemies and later story warnings.

Reveal the region guide · later-game spoilers
The authors’ overview of the tower
Floors / regionWhat to expect
1–10 · Skeleton corpsComparatively weak enemies teach basic tactics. The Skeleton carrying a sword and shield is a troublesome opponent.
11–20 · Immortal forceZombies and Vampires are powerful; the Cross is valuable against them. A Giant Octopus blocks the route and guards a special reward.
21–30 · Great Magic MasterThis region’s boss is very strong. The authors advise patience; there is comparatively little else here.
31–40 · Golden Knight corpsKnights, swordsmen and soldiers make this a tough region. The Golden Knight is an unreliable speaker; a Giant Dragon presents another obstacle.
41–50 · Magic Sergeant ZenoMagical enemies dominate. Zeno orchestrated the hero’s capture in the introduction. The original help warns that trying to fight this final opponent head-on will lead to destruction.

Based on: TSW.txt, “The explanation of each area” / Tsw.hlp, “Area Explanation”

Click a character to read its introduction, just as in the original help. You can also use Tab, then Enter or Space.
